Content:
Consider the following diagram.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/900da63e2c543704c5cc2e7f43b86aaa]

Content:
The points [MATH: A,B,C,] and [MATH: D] lie on the circle, and the secant lines [MATH: \overleftrightarrow{AB}] and [MATH: \overleftrightarrow{CD}] intersect at the point [MATH: P] in the circle's exterior, as shown.

Content:
We're also given that

Content:
[MATH: m\overset{\frown}{AC} =80^\circ, \qquad m\overset{\frown}{BD} = 26^\circ.]

Content:
Note that [MATH: \angle P] is called a secant-secant angle because it's the angle formed by the intersection of two secants.

Content:
It can be shown that the measure of [MATH: \angle P] is half the difference between the measures of the larger and smaller intercepted arcs:

Content:
[MATH: m∠P = (mAC^(⌢) − mBD^(⌢))/(2)]

Content:
This is called the secant-secant angle theorem. We'll prove this theorem at the end of the lesson.

Content:
So, by substituting the numbers from above, we get

Content:
[MATH: m∠P|= (80^{∘} − 26^{∘})/(2) = 27^{∘}.]

Content:
Sometimes, two secant lines intersect at a circle's interior. In such cases, we use a different method to calculate the measure of the secant-secant angle.

Content:
Consider the following diagram.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/1832b20dd2fafd5aeffbdfd37fb5ee15]

Content:
The points [MATH: A, B, C,] and [MATH: D] lie on the circle, and the secant lines [MATH: \overleftrightarrow{AB}] and [MATH: \overleftrightarrow{CD}] intersect at the point [MATH: Q] in the circle's interior, as shown.

Content:
Note that since [MATH: \angle AQC] and [MATH: \angle BQD] are vertical angles, we have that

Content:
[MATH: m\angle AQC = m\angle BQD.]

Content:
It can be shown that the measure of the angles formed by these secant lines is half the sum of the measures of the intercepted arcs.

Content:
[MATH: m∠AQC = m∠BQD = (mAC^(⌢) + mBD^(⌢))/(2)]

Content:
In other words, the measure of the secant-secant angles is the average of the measures of the intercepted arcs.

Content:
We'll prove this formula at the end of the lesson.

Also, since [MATH: \angle ADC] and [MATH: \angle BAD] are inscribed angles, we have that

Item 6 — Tutorial: Secant-Secant Angles Within the Circles Interior

Content:

Content:
Note that since [MATH: \angle AQC] and [MATH: \angle BQD] are vertical angles, we have that

Content:
[MATH: m\angle AQC = m\angle BQD.]

Content:
It can be shown that the measure of the angles formed by these secant lines is half the sum of the measures of the intercepted arcs.

Content:
[MATH: m∠AQC = m∠BQD = (mAC^(⌢) + mBD^(⌢))/(2)]

Content:
In other words, the measure of the secant-secant angles is the average of the measures of the intercepted arcs.

Content:
We'll prove this formula at the end of the lesson.

Item 13 — Tutorial: Proving the Secant-Secant Angles Theorem: Exterior Angle Case
